- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward slightly to account for mean reversion or momentum.
- Overshoot after high-value spikes (e.g., >70) by 2–5 points; cap or dampen forecast peaks.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; smooth transitions between high and low values.
- Forecast mean often lags true mean by 3–7 days; shift forecast slightly forward to align with observed trend.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; reduce weight on last 5–7 days if they show erratic or non-representative behavior.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- Forecast often underestimates low-value tail events (e.g., <65) — increase sensitivity to low-end volatility.
